notes:
Quick summary: Sentinel Edge is evaluating Redwood Private for sensitive threat intel enrichment and triage automation. Primary driver = ability to run in VPC with customer-managed KMS + strong, exportable audit logs for SIEM ingestion. CISO quote: 'We need forensic-grade logs, 7+ year retention, and a clear schema we can map into Splunk/ECS.' SecOps wants both streaming export (Splunk HEC / syslog over TLS) and S3 archive option. Key ask: sample log schema, examples of PII redaction/retention controls, confirmation of KV cache not persisting plaintext prompts to disk, and how model input/output are categorized in logs.

- Logging specifics requested by SecOps:
  • Export formats: JSON (ECS-friendly), Common Event Format (CEF) for legacy SIEM, syslog over TLS
  • Required fields: timestamp (ISO8601), tenant_id, request_id, user_id (hashed), model_version, model_variant, prompt_hash, response_hash, token_count, latency_ms, decision_path, api_route, src_ip, action (inference/embedding/rerank), status, error_code, kms_key_id
  • Access logs: separate admin/audit stream (login, key-usage, role changes), separate model-invocation stream
  • Retention: minimum 7 years for audit logs; 90 days for raw request payloads unless flagged for incident review
  • SIEM integration patterns: preferred = direct HEC endpoint + signed requests; fallback = S3 -> Kinesis Firehose -> Splunk; also support for Datadog Logs intake and Sumo Logic
  • Real-time alerts: must surface anomalous access patterns (excessive token volumes, unknown principal) via webhook to SOAR

- KMS/crypto requirements:
  • Customer-managed CMKs in AWS KMS (preferably asymmetric for signing), optional HSM module for key ceremony
  • Key rotation policy support and key usage audit logs exported to SIEM
  • Clear separation: keys for encryption-at-rest vs. keys for request-level envelope encryption

- Data residency/compliance:
  • Tenant data must remain in selected region (us-east-1) for regulatory reasons
  • Audit trails must not cross-region unless explicit replication request made

- POC scope agreed:
  • 2-week POC in customer VPC peered with Redwood test VPC
  • Deliverables: sample audit log stream to customer's Splunk HEC, S3 archive with 90-day lifecycle rule, log schema doc, end-to-end diagram
  • Success criteria: logs delivered with required fields, no plaintext prompts written to persistent disk, KMS integration using customer CMK

- Quotes/paraphrases from calls:
  • CISO: 'Forensic parity with our SIEM is non-negotiable.'
  • SecOps lead: 'Show me the exact JSON payload — we will map it into our ECS fields.'

Next steps / immediate asks:
- Provide formal log schema doc (ECS mapping + example events) — due 2026-03-10
- Provide architecture diagram for VPC peering, NAT, and KMS onboarding
- Confirm support for Splunk HEC token rotation and HEC over TLS
- Provide draft DPA & security addendum for legal review

Open questions / blockers in detail:
- Legal wants language around KMS split control and incident key disclosure process
- Network has quarterly maintenance window; peering needs to be scheduled for May
- Finance needs a one-page SOW + pricing for 12-month committed Dedicated + Private option
